subtype: Approach: tempted by a gift or sweet [Pitfall]
passage:
Monday. Rekha Ma'am talked to Class Five about strangers. "A gift is never a reason to go anywhere with someone," she said. Zain doodled in his notebook.
Wednesday. After school a man at the lane offered him chocolate and a turn on a video game. "Just come and see something in the lane." Zain stared at the shiny wrapper and took a step. His friend Simran grabbed his sleeve. "Remember Monday? Come on!" They ran to the school gate.
Thursday. Zain told Rekha Ma'am, who wrote it all down and phoned his mother before lunch. He was still ashamed that he had nearly gone.

qa.q: Who grabbed Zain's sleeve in the lane?
qa.a: His friend Simran grabbed his sleeve.

qa.q: What was Zain feeling when he stared at the shiny wrapper?
qa.a: Tempted and eager for the treat, so his caution weakened and he took a step.

qa.q: What could Zain do next time he is offered a gift, and why?
qa.a: He could say no, step away and tell a trusted adult straight away, because a reward is not a reason to go anywhere.

qa.q: How does Simran see the offer in the lane?
qa.a: Simran recognises the situation Rekha Ma'am warned about and acts at once by pulling Zain away and running to the gate.

grounding: A boy tempted by a treat from a stranger takes a step, until his friend reminds him of the school safety talk.

subtype: Approach: tempted by a gift or sweet [Pitfall]
passage: Zubin, you're laughing at the safety talk? Let your Akash Chacha tell you about the day it saved me. I was a boy, walking home with my friend Nitin, when a man near the lane called us. "Want chocolates? And I have a new video game at my place, just down there. Come and see." Chocolate! A new game! I actually took a step. My feet wanted to go. Nitin grabbed my collar. "Akash! Remember the talk. Never go with anyone for a treat." I stopped. It was like waking up. We ran straight to the paan shop where Nitin's father sat, and told him. He stood up at once, took us home, and went to the police that same evening.

qa.q: What did the man offer the boys?
qa.a: Chocolates and a new video game.

qa.q: How did young Akash feel when he took a step toward the man?
qa.a: Young Akash felt tempted and excited by the reward, which pushed caution away for a moment.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story, and why did it matter?
qa.a: Nitin grabbing the collar and reminding Akash of the safety talk was the turning point, because it broke the pull of the reward before Akash went further.

qa.q: How might Nitin's father have seen the boys running up?
qa.a: Nitin's father would have been alarmed and protective, acting at once to take them home and go to the police.

grounding: An elder recalls, as a boy, being tempted by a man's offer of chocolate and a game until a friend reminded him of the school safety talk.

subtype: Approach: tempted by a gift or sweet [Pitfall]
passage: The school bus was forty minutes late, and the teachers had gone inside because of the heat, so Joseph and Kashish waited by the wall. A man they didn't know came over. "I've got a box of chocolates and a new game console in that lane. Come see, just for a minute." Joseph felt the pull. He loved that console. He started to stand up. Kashish said sharply, "Joseph. The safety talk. Treats from strangers means no." Joseph sat back down, cheeks hot. The man shrugged and walked off. The two boys went straight inside to the staffroom and told the teacher on duty. She called their parents and the principal, and the school informed the police that afternoon.

qa.q: How late was the school bus?
How did Joseph feel when Kashish reminded him of the safety talk?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed, with hot cheeks, having been tempted by the console.

qa.q: What else could the school change after this?
qa.a: The school could keep a teacher at the gate until every bus arrives, so children are never left waiting alone.

qa.q: How does the moment look to Kashish?
qa.a: Kashish sees a friend being tempted and speaks up sharply, probably feeling worried and protective.

grounding: It shows a boy tempted by an offer of chocolate and a game to go to a lane, until his friend reminds him of the school safety talk.
